IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields signal bond-market trends. Trend followers have typically held long fixed-income positions, so rate declines feed directly into their returns.

B.rationale: Widening spreads together with weak high-yield returns mark deteriorating credit. Such episodes tend to become persistent risk-off trends that time-series momentum strategies exploit.

V.rationale: Elevated equity volatility accompanies extended market dislocations, when trend-following returns have been documented to be strongest (crisis alpha).

AP.rationale: Equity index futures are a large part of CTA books, so sustained equity trends feed into performance.

ST.rationale: Cross-sectional momentum shares trend-continuation exposure with time-series momentum. Strong UMD signals an environment where trends persist.

FX.rationale: Directional dollar moves are a major source of trend-following P&L across currency futures.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity moves capture trending conditions in a sizeable part of CTA portfolios.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions are associated with prolonged deleveraging trends across asset classes, which CTAs harvest.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent strategy returns indicate that trends are established in its markets, which may persist over the horizon.

IR.rationale: Sharp rises in intermediate yields are rate shocks that hit levered long-bond positions and raise strategy variance.

B.rationale: Credit spread widening signals rising risk across markets and larger subsequent price swings in CTA holdings.

V.rationale: Simultaneously high equity and gold implied volatility indicates broad cross-asset uncertainty. That carries forward-looking information about volatility in multi-asset futures books.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs raise subsequent volatility through the leverage effect, and they force CTA position changes.

ST.rationale: Weak momentum returns signal trend reversals, during which trend-following positions are whipsawed and variance rises.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation reflects safe-haven flows and carry unwinds that bring abrupt cross-asset moves.

COM.rationale: Oil price drops are often disorderly and spill over into energy and commodity futures volatility.

MC.rationale: Financial stress is associated with elevated and persistent volatility across asset classes.

ENDG.rationale: High recent realised variance may mean-revert or persist beyond its baseline forecast. The model learns which.

IR.rationale: Abrupt bond sell-offs hurt the typically long-duration positions of trend followers and can produce large losses.

B.rationale: A sharp credit rebound marks a risk-on reversal of prior defensive trends, the classic loss state for CTAs.

V.rationale: High volatility widens the return distribution and raises the chance of sharp trend reversals.

AP.rationale: Strong equity rallies, especially after declines, catch trend followers positioned short or defensively.

ST.rationale: Weak momentum together with strong short-term reversal is the momentum-crash state, when trend-continuation strategies suffer their largest losses.

FX.rationale: Dollar reversals unwind established currency trends and generate losses on trend-following FX positions.

COM.rationale: Sharp oil rebounds reverse commodity trends and inflict losses on short energy positions.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise the likelihood of policy-driven reversals and disorderly markets that produce tail losses.

ENDG.rationale: After strong runs, crowded trends are more exposed to abrupt reversals.

IR.rationale: Bond rallies during flight-to-quality episodes deliver outsized gains to long-duration trend positions.

B.rationale: Deteriorating credit marks persistent risk-off trends, in which CTAs have historically earned their largest gains.

V.rationale: Crisis periods with high equity volatility coincide with the convex, crisis-alpha payoff of trend following.

AP.rationale: Extended equity declines generate strong trends and are documented as the best environment for managed futures.

ST.rationale: Strong momentum indicates trend persistence, raising the chance of outsized trend-following gains.

FX.rationale: Strong dollar rallies in risk-off phases create large, persistent currency trends.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity sell-offs tend to trend strongly and reward short commodity positions.

MC.rationale: Rising financial stress is associated with prolonged deleveraging trends across assets that CTAs capture.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent returns indicate trends are established and may extend into large gains.
